question: Can we construct a deterministic public synthetic Kubernetes metric workload with explicit 3-hour node turnover, pod churn, HPA changes, realistic label selectors and distinct stable-versus-churning series for later native ClickHouse/VM tests?
baseline: Existing canonical 1.33m Jenkins fixture and native R03 stock O1 comparison; this phase does not claim a performance baseline
candidate: New deterministic streaming Kubernetes workload generator plus pure-Python oracle and small CI smoke; no C++ patch or expensive ClickHouse build
fixture: Public synthetic node/pod/service metric families; user-configurable count and scrape/node lifetimes; fixed seed; emit SHA256 for entire fixture; no private telemetry
single_variable: Workload distribution and churn (fixture design); no query performance intervention in this phase
math_bound: At n stable node slots, scrape period s, duration T, one node incarnation every L seconds per slot: node incarnations ≈ n*T/L, sample events O(n*T/s*(node-label-series + active pod-label-series)); deterministic bounded-size smoke before full load
falsifier: Generator not reproducible; nonmonotone counters within one series, invalid reset, duplicate metric+tag+timestamp keys, incorrect HPA pod reuse, unbounded peak RAM for a streaming generator, or no independently verifiable sample/series counts
test_matrix: Pure Python tests: deterministic bytes and manifest SHA; node rotation with stagger, pod HPA extra replica ID changes, stable service series, monotonically increasing counters per series; sample count and output shape; small CI 16 slots 6h, no ClickHouse binary
runner_budget: One low-cost GitHub Actions smoke job, python3 only, <5 minutes; no expensive builds; full 400-node 14d generation deferred
planned_workflow: .github/workflows/ts-lab-r01-kubernetes-fixture.yml; unique path-scoped push; no schedule, no cancellation
